settings.heading: Wearing an Eternity Ring in a Stack

settings.content: Four arrangements, and the fit checks that stop rings damaging each other

settings.heading: Most Eternity Rings Are Worn Alongside Something
settings.body:
Very few eternity rings are worn alone, and how they sit against the existing pair matters more than most people expect. Two diamond bands rubbing directly against each other will damage both, slowly and invisibly, over years.

What follows are the common arrangements. They are options rather than rules, and no order is more correct than another whatever anyone tells you.

settings.heading: Worn alone
settings.body: On its own finger or its own hand. No compromises on width, height or presence, and nothing to rub against.
settings.label: Option one

settings.heading: Above the engagement ring
settings.body: Wedding ring closest to the hand, engagement ring above it, eternity ring outermost. The most common arrangement.
settings.label: Option two

settings.heading: In the middle
settings.body: Eternity ring between the wedding and engagement rings, which frames the engagement ring and keeps the wedding band closest to the heart.
settings.label: Option three

settings.heading: On the other hand
settings.body: Keeps the eternity ring entirely clear of the existing pair. Worth considering if the stack is becoming tight or the rings do not sit well together.
settings.label: Option four

settings.intro: No order is more correct than another. Choose the one that sits comfortably and looks right to you.
settings.heading: Where It Can Sit

settings.label: Match or deliberately contrast the metal
settings.note: A near-match reads as a mistake. Identical or obviously different both work.

settings.label: Compare profile height, not only width
settings.note: Two rings of the same width can sit at quite different heights and refuse to sit flush.

settings.label: Check what touches what
settings.note: Exposed diamond girdles, claws and channel edges against an adjacent ring will wear both.

settings.label: Look for obstructions
settings.note: A low basket, halo, trilogy side stones or shoulders can prevent a straight band sitting close.

settings.label: Check with fingers closed
settings.note: Rings that sit beautifully with the hand open can press uncomfortably when the fingers are together.

settings.label: Consider the combined width
settings.note: Several individually comfortable rings can feel tight as a stack, particularly in warm weather.

settings.intro: Most stacking problems are predictable, and all six of these can be checked before anything is made.
settings.heading: Six Fit Checks
Spacers Are a Design Choice
settings.body:
A slim plain spacer ring prevents direct contact where an eternity setting would otherwise rub an engagement ring basket or another diamond band. It protects both rings, and it can be finished to disappear almost entirely between them.

People sometimes resist the idea because it feels like an extra ring solving a problem. In practice it is cheaper than repairing two damaged bands, and it often improves how the stack sits.

settings.eyebrow: If the Rings Will Not Sit Together
settings.heading: Shaping Is the Other Answer
settings.body: Where a spacer will not solve it, a shaped or fitted band made to follow the engagement ring's outline usually will. It is more work than a straight band but it is the difference between a stack that is worn and one that is not.

settings.q: What order should I wear my rings in?
settings.a: Tradition puts the wedding band closest to the heart, so wedding ring first, then engagement ring, then eternity ring outermost. Plenty of people wear them differently and it makes no practical difference unless a band is shaped, in which case it only works one way.

settings.q: Will my rings damage each other?
settings.a: They can, particularly where exposed diamond girdles or claws sit against another band. Diamond is hard enough to abrade gold and platinum steadily. A slim spacer between them prevents it, and an annual inspection catches it early.

settings.q: Should the eternity ring match the wedding band?
settings.a: Match it, or contrast it obviously. The combination that rarely works is a near-match, where the metals or widths are only slightly different and the effect reads as accidental rather than deliberate.

settings.q: My stack feels tight in summer. Is that normal?
settings.a: Yes. Several individually comfortable rings can press together as fingers swell. If it happens regularly, wearing one on the other hand is the simplest fix, and it is worth checking the fit before assuming a resize is needed.

settings.q: Can I add an eternity ring years later?
settings.a: Of course, and most people do, usually for an anniversary or a birth. It is easier if the wedding band was chosen with a future stack in mind, but we can almost always find something that sits well, including shaping it if needed.
